stem: $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle in which $AB = AC = {=legs}$ cm and $BC = {=base}$ cm. Find $m(\angle A)$ in degrees, to two decimal places.
solution: Draw $\overrightarrow{AD} \perp \overline{BC}$. Since the triangle is isosceles, $D$ is the midpoint of $\overline{BC}$, so $BD = {=hk}$ cm.
notes: Triangles (5,6),(13,10),(5,8) scaled by k. B=arccos(3/5)=53.1301, A=73.7398; arccos(5/13)=67.3801, A=45.2397; arccos(4/5)=36.8699, A=106.2602. Computed from unrounded B then rounded; matches 180-2*rounded B too.
